BIBLIOGRAPHY: Almandary, J. Peradaban di Daerah Mamasa: Kajian Budaya Austronesia di Situs Dambu dan Matti (The Beginning Civilization in the Mamasa Area: the Austronesian Culture Study in Sites of Dambu and Matti).
COMMENTS: Description: According to the oral tradition of the Mamasa community, particularly those settled in the Balla area, the Dambu site was the earliest settlement of their ancestors before they moved to the Matti and Paku areas. Much of the site surface is still covered with grass, making it very difficult to find artefacts on the surface. Archaeological finds were limited to areas of ground already cultivated for growing vegetables or tubers. A survey recovered stone flake artefacts bearing clear traces of use, evidenced by technological characteristics including a bulbus on the ventral face, a striking platform on the proximal end, and a dorsal flaking surface worked obliquely to both sides forming two thin cutting edges. The cutting edges show retouch and fine edge damage from intensive use.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Almandary, J. Peradaban di Daerah Mamasa: Kajian Budaya Austronesia di Situs Dambu dan Matti (The Beginning Civilization in the Mamasa Area: the Austronesian Culture Study in Sites of Dambu and Matti).
COMMENTS: Description: One of the significant find types at the Dambu-Matti sites is stone flake artefacts. Technologically they demonstrate flaking techniques including a striking platform, bulbus, and cutting edges. Two flake artefacts were recovered from excavation and one from surface survey. Flake I measures 3.8 cm in length, 2.3 cm in width at the midpoint, and 0.9 cm in thickness.
